title: Wide-field view of the sky around VFTS 102: the fastest rotating massive star
caption: The sky around VFTS 102 in the Tarantula Nebula, imaged by ESO's MPG/ESO 2.2-metre and VISTA telescopes

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: At the centre of this wide view lies the brilliant star VFTS 102. Around it spreads part of the Tarantula Nebula, a stellar nursery in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a small neighbouring galaxy of the Milky Way.

No star has been found spinning faster than VFTS 102. It is described as brilliant, and here it sits right at the centre of the frame, with the gas and stars of the Tarantula Nebula spread out around it.

The picture blends visible-light and infrared images from two telescopes in Chile: the 2.2-metre MPG/ESO telescope at La Silla, via its Wide Field Imager, and the 4.1-metre VISTA infrared survey telescope at Paranal. Blending visible and infrared light in this way gives a single, combined view of the region around the star.

understand.summary: This composite combines visible-light images from the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope with near-infrared images from VISTA; the colour mapping isn't published.
